prompt: A partner integration says the signature on the webhooks we send them never validates on their side. What exactly are we signing, and with what algorithm, so I can tell them how to verify it?
rationale: The shape where the obvious grep term is spread across several files and the answer lives in only one. Grepping 'sign' or 'signature' in the fixture hits four files: src/notify/webhook.ts (sets the x-signature header), src/api/middleware.ts (reads the x-signature header), src/auth/token.ts (defines sign and verify) and, via near-miss on 'send failed', src/notify/email.ts. Only src/auth/token.ts answers the question: sign() is createHmac("sha256", secret).update(payload).digest("hex"). src/notify/webhook.ts supplies the other half - the signed payload is JSON.stringify(event), the same string sent as the request body, and the header is x-signature. The strongest trap is src/api/middleware.ts: it uses the identical header name for the OPPOSITE direction (verifying inbound requests), so an agent that stops at the first x-signature hit describes inbound auth and answers the wrong question. src/auth/session.ts and src/auth/scopes.ts sit in the same directory as the answer and are irrelevant. Grounding is enforced because HMAC-SHA256 is the industry-default webhook scheme - Stripe, GitHub and Shopify all use it - so a model can emit the right algorithm with no retrieval at all. The answer must name createHmac / token.ts / webhook.ts / node:crypto, or the transcript must show src/auth/token.ts being opened. Asserting any other primitive (RSA, Ed25519, JWT, SHA-1, SHA-512, asymmetric keys) in a non-contrastive sentence fails. Verified against the live rank tool over all 45 fixture files: present 96%, with src/auth/token.ts first (score 0.860) and src/notify/webhook.ts second (0.140) - the two files the answer actually needs - while the same-header decoy src/api/middleware.ts falls to fourth at 0.000.
_answer: HMAC-SHA256 over JSON.stringify(event), hex-encoded, in the x-signature header. sign() in src/auth/token.ts, called from deliver() in src/notify/webhook.ts.
